clue.text: People engaged in trade may well be nameless

indicators.note: 'may well be' suggests the following word could turn into something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Traders, perhaps, often go about anonymously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may well be' is the anagram signal: NAMELESS rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Salespeople are those whose job is selling goods, i.e. engaged in commerce.

clue.text: Satirical pieces about the right wear for women

indicators.note: the satirical pieces go around the letter for right, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: skits are short comic or satirical sketches

explanation.surface: Satirical sketches about what women ought to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SKITS round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirts are garments traditionally worn by women, hanging from the waist.

clue.text: Family junk

definitions.meaning: a brood of young born to one animal at one time

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a set of offspring born together and discarded rubbish.

clue.text: County sets with more potential

indicators.note: 'potential' says the letters have the capacity to become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A county whose sets have greater promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' is the anagram signal: SETS and MORE rearranged give the answer, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a county in south-west England.

clue.text: A painter getting involved in a petty quarrel

indicators.note: the painter is said to be involved in the words that follow, so his name is found within them

explanation.surface: An artist caught up in a trivial dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was an English painter of the 19th century, known for nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty (1787-1849) was an English artist celebrated for his figure studies.

clue.text: Sounds second-hand!

parts.note: read as noises heard a second time, bounced back off a wall, rather than goods sold used

explanation.surface: A remark that some sounds, like used goods, are not new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second-hand' suggests used goods; here it means sounds heard again after reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflected sound reaches the listener a second time, repeated by a surface such as a cliff.

clue.text: Prison's not so hot!

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a jail and also means chillier.

clue.text: Being ostentatious about silver, many caused offence

indicators.note: the showy word goes around the symbol for silver, enclosing it

parts.note: outré means extravagantly unconventional, flamboyant
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Flaunting silver, a crowd gave offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AG inside OUTRE; D (500) for 'many' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To have outraged someone is to have shocked or affronted them.

clue.text: Look over a range that's less lavish

parts.note: to scan is to look over quickly
a tier is a row or rank, such as seats in a range

explanation.surface: Examining a cooker that is less extravagant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' suggests a cooker or mountains; here it is a row or level, TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Scantier means more meagre, sparser, so less generous or abundant.

clue.text: Very friendly at getting in eventually

indicators.note: the word 'at' is said to get inside the phrase for 'eventually', so it is placed within it

parts.note: 'in time' means eventually, sooner or later
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who becomes very friendly once finally admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' puts AT inside IN TIME, giving IN-TIM-AT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate describes a close, personal relationship, one that is warmly familiar.

clue.text: Left one to appear before a judge

definitions.text: Left one to appear before a judge

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned to face a judge in court.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT + I + A; the whole clue also describes Shakespeare's Portia, who appears before the Duke disguised as a lawyer in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Merchant of Venice the heroine pleads in court before the Duke, posing as a young doctor of law.

clue.text: Officer taking care of money an individual left

parts.note: c/o is the abbreviation for care of on letters
L stands for pound (libra), British money
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: An officer looking after the cash a single person bequeathed.
explanation.walkthrough: L for pound comes from the Latin libra, the source of the £ sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army commissioned rank.

clue.text: The presumption of the fellow in the right!

indicators.note: the man is put in the political party, so the word for him goes inside the other word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's right-wing Conservative Party
a fellow is a 'he'

explanation.surface: Asking what the man on the political right is assuming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the right' is a common crossword stand-in for Britain's Conservative Party, whose members are nicknamed Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition or hypothesis, something assumed but not proven.

clue.text: Promise made by witches to a worker

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A pledge given by a group of witches to an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is a common crossword signal for ANT (or BEE), after the worker caste of the insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a solemn agreement or binding pledge.

clue.text: New store is to reorganise accounts

indicators.note: a new form of the words is wanted, so their letters are rearranged
reorganising the letters of the words puts them in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new shop is going to restructure its finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' and 'to reorganise' are both anagram signals: STORE IS rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories are narratives or reports, tales of events.

clue.text: Cut once it's badly affected

indicators.note: something badly affected is damaged and disordered, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something cut when damaged in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly affected' is the anagram signal: ONCE IT'S rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a slice or part cut from a whole, as in a cross-section.

clue.text: Only calling for a couple of notes

indicators.note: calling out means saying the notes aloud, so the answer is how they sound

parts.note: mi and re are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Asking for only two musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' signals a homophone: the sol-fa notes MI RE, said aloud, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, as in 'a mere child', i.e. simply.

clue.text: The boards propose a top man

parts.note: to plan is to intend or propose
a king is the man at the top of a kingdom

explanation.surface: The board of directors suggests a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boards' suggests a board of directors; here it is wooden planks collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: Planking is a set of planks, as in a floor or ship's deck.

clue.text: Spiked reeds possibly for planting around public gardens

indicators.note: the letters for the reeds are placed around the gardens, as if planted round them
'possibly' says the word may appear in another form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Kew Gardens are the Royal Botanic Gardens in London

explanation.surface: Reeds sharpened, perhaps, for planting in a public park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spiked' looks like an adjective about the reeds but defines the answer; 'possibly' scrambles the reeds and 'planting around' wraps them round London's Royal Botanic Gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewered means pierced with a pointed rod, impaled.

clue.text: Break without ever showing much respect

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside means the break goes around 'ever'

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
taken as written

explanation.surface: Breaking the rules without ever being respectful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking', so the break surrounds the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means deeply respectful, deferential.

clue.text: Similar to relish

definitions.meaning: to relish something is to enjoy or be fond of it

explanation.definitionFit: One word means resembling (a preposition) and also to enjoy (a verb).

clue.text: Tidied up when required

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both arranging things neatly and having commanded something to be done.

clue.text: Stick given as business present

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A stick handed over as a business gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' suggests a gift; here it means in attendance, HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together, adhere.

clue.text: Beat into a thin plate

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit
a shortened form, 'in' for into

explanation.surface: Hammer something until it becomes a thin sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat into' looks like metalworking; LAM is an informal word for beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamina is a thin layer, sheet or scale.

clue.text: Fed-up — aim for safeguard

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is written bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Fed up, and looking to protect oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed-up' looks like boredom; 'up' reverses FED to DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend is to protect or guard against attack.

clue.text: Late arrival could make men cower

indicators.note: 'could make' says the following letters can be reworked to form a new word

explanation.surface: Someone arriving late might frighten the men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' is the anagram signal: MEN COWER rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer is someone who has only recently arrived somewhere.

clue.text: Report of some soldiers overdue

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
late means behind time

explanation.surface: An account by some soldiers who have not turned up on time.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate is to tell or narrate an account of events.

clue.text: The old queen accomplished nothing

parts.note: did means accomplished, carried out
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The former queen achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido was the legendary queen of Carthage in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the mythical founder and ruler of Carthage.

clue.text: New serial set in a foreign country

indicators.note: a new version of the word is made by reordering its letters

explanation.surface: A new television serial filmed abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal: SERIAL rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation in the Middle East, foreign to a British setter.

clue.text: Salvation is seen by the fortune-teller

definitions.meaning: a means of rescue in a crisis
a palmist reads a crease on the hand thought to show how long one will live

explanation.surface: A palm reader finds rescue in what they see.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a rope or support that saves someone and the palmistry crease said to foretell longevity.

clue.text: Puff after middle-age and obtain this useful device

indicators.note: the promotional piece is placed after the letter taken from 'age'
the clue asks for the central part of the word 'age', its middle letter

parts.note: a puff is a promotional notice, an advertisement or ad
to obtain is to get

explanation.surface: Middle-aged, take a breath and buy this handy tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puff' suggests breathing but means an advert here; 'middle' takes the central letter of 'age', and 'after' puts the advert behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small mechanical contrivance or handy tool.

clue.text: Place where drinks are of some help

parts.note: port is a fortified wine, so ports are drinks
aid is assistance

explanation.surface: A spot where drinking proves rather useful.
explanation.walkthrough: Port Said is an Egyptian city at the north end of the Suez Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Said is a city in Egypt, a geographical location.
